O Cervello BPMS era uma plataforma perso: Cervello BPMS was a customizable platform for IT management and support tickets. When I joined the project in 2018, the interface had grown without dedicated design support. Built by developers on a Bootstrap template, it worked, but looked dated, presented a lot of information, and relied heavily on tabs for navigation.
Durante aproximadamente quatro anos, fui: For approximately four years, I was the team’s only designer. I worked on UX/UI, prototyping, evaluating designs with users, and creating the design system. I also wrote HTML, CSS, and SCSS to support implementation.
O desafio era dar mais clareza ao produt: The challenge was to make the product clearer and create a foundation for future development while preserving the features and customization customers valued.
Conversas com usuários, PM e equipe come: Conversations with users, the product manager, and the sales team showed that each new need tended to become another field, control, or feature. Over time, this accumulation weakened the visual hierarchy and created inconsistencies across modules.
Informações importantes competiam com de: Important information competed with secondary details. Tabs split tasks across hidden areas and made navigation harder, especially for people unfamiliar with the system.
Os profissionais de suporte e TI usavam: Support and IT professionals mainly used the platform to look up, handle, transfer, and close tickets. Reviewing history, the knowledge base, and metrics came next. Together with the product manager, I prioritized the path from
Começava pelo fluxo principal de cada ár: I started with each area’s main flow, then worked through settings, states, and exceptions. On the home page, this included customizing the page and its shortcuts. For tickets, it meant exploring actions such as forwarding, changing status, and closing in more detail.
Um processo próximo de usuários e desenv: Working closely with users and developers
As propostas eram discutidas com usuário: We used prototypes to discuss proposals with users. These conversations were qualitative and informal, without a rigid test script. Alongside their reactions to the screens, users shared other difficulties they faced with the platform.
O trabalho seguia um ciclo de: The work followed a cycle of
protótipo, validação com usuários, alinh: prototyping, evaluating designs with users, aligning with the product manager and developers, and implementing the designs in HTML/SCSS
. Essa proximidade ajudava a ajustar as: . This close collaboration helped us adapt solutions to people’s needs and the product’s technical constraints.
Como produto white label, o Cervello pre: As a white-label product, Cervello needed to reflect different customers’ brands. I created a palette with predefined text-to-background relationships and code-generated color variations for controls.
As cores de sucesso, alerta e erro perma: Success, warning, and error colors stayed fixed. This allowed the branding to change without changing the meaning of interface states.
Defini uma escala tipográfica com Roboto: I defined a type scale using Roboto and standardized icons with Font Awesome. On each screen or modal, I reserved the primary-color button for the most important action.
Títulos mais informativos, agrupamentos,: More informative headings, groupings, borders, and dividers helped users understand where they were and how content was organized. These rules brought consistency to the screens without requiring every module to look the same.
Em algumas áreas, uma página vertical ma: In some areas, a longer vertical page worked better than multiple tabs. It kept content visible and let users search with the browser’s built-in find feature.
Em outras, fazia mais sentido dividir o: Elsewhere, it made more sense to break the work into steps, use modals, or reorder records to show the most recent ones first. The choice depended on the task and the clearest way to present its information.
A redução das abas deixou algumas página: Reducing tabs moved some pages deeper into the navigation. To make them easier to reach, I proposed a universal search in the header: users could find a ticket from the home page by entering its number.
O PM complementou a proposta com breadcr: The product manager added breadcrumbs to show the path to the current page. Each module also received its own navigation and context cues, such as ticket statuses, a navigation tree in the knowledge base, and assignee information on the Kanban board.
Um Design System que cresceu com o produ: A design system that grew with the product
O sistema de design nasceu das telas. Pr: The design system emerged from the screens. I first explored a visual direction with the product manager. As the solutions took shape, I organized recurring elements into a reusable foundation:
Botões, espaçamentos, bordas e arredonda: Buttons, spacing, borders, and corner radii.
Ao começar uma nova tela, reutilizava es: When starting a new screen, I reused this foundation and assessed what needed a dedicated solution. Tickets, dashboards, projects, and the knowledge base shared the same fundamentals while using controls suited to their tasks.
Depois de consolidar a home e a tela pri: After consolidating the home page and main ticket screen, I estimate that around 80% of the visual structure needed for new modules was already in place. Since I also wrote the styles, that reuse extended to the code.
A home combinava atalhos em cards, widge: The home page combined shortcut cards, optional widgets, a background image, and drag-and-drop organization. I also designed a settings screen with a preview before publishing.
A personalização dos cards trazia um des: Card customization introduced a challenge: each customer would need to choose images and content. I proposed a library of royalty-free images, already sized and related to IT topics such as servers and meeting rooms. This made initial setup easier.
Foi uma das áreas mais trabalhosas do pr: This was one of the most demanding areas of the project. I would revisit some visual choices today, but the solution met the business requirements and the need for customization.
Os dashboards já existiam; meu foco foi: The dashboards already existed; my focus was improving their composition and presentation. Users could choose metrics, chart types, grid space, and component order, and switch between light and dark modes.
Trabalhei com a biblioteca JavaScript já: I worked with the JavaScript library the team was already using. The prototypes and CSS respected its limitations while adapting the appearance to the new visual system.
O módulo de projetos recebeu uma interfa: The projects module received a Kanban interface with its own elements, such as task assignee identification. It showed how the same visual foundation could accommodate different needs within the product.
Os mesmos componentes em modo claro e es: The same components in light and dark modes: charts, counters, and information blocks share a grid. The values shown are interface examples, not measures of the redesign’s impact.
O aplicativo funcionava como uma webview: The app ran in a webview, and the company wanted to offer almost all of the platform’s important capabilities on mobile. Most of the adaptation came from the responsive component structure, with specific adjustments for readability.
Defendi uma prioridade menor no mobile p: I advocated giving home page configuration and dashboard creation lower priority on mobile. These tasks were more common during system rollout than in support professionals’ daily work.
O time era enxuto e não tinha um desenvo: The team was small and had no dedicated front-end developer. I therefore replaced much of Bootstrap with a custom SCSS foundation, organizing components with BEM and using styles that generated the different white-label color options.
Algumas propostas precisaram ser revista: Some proposals needed revision because of backend limitations, such as search fields in service scheduling. In those cases, we adapted the experience to what the architecture could support.
Também revisava a implementação e mantin: I also reviewed the implementation and kept the prototype updated as things changed, so that Figma continued to reflect the delivered product.

Lista mobile de solicitações com ações d: Mobile request list with approval actions
Home, solicitações e busca no aplicativo: Home, requests, and search in the app. These screens show one example of the platform’s customizable branding.
O redesign recebeu avaliações positivas: The redesign received positive feedback from users involved in validation, the product manager, and the sales team. Customization made it easier to present the platform to different customers.
Não havia telemetria sistemática para me: There was no systematic telemetry to measure task time, errors, or adoption, partly because many customers used on-premises installations. New contracts were signed during this period, but I do not have data to attribute them to the redesign. The results I could observe were mainly qualitative.
O Cervello me mostrou como o design pode: Cervello showed me how design can help a complex platform evolve: by organizing information, guiding navigation, and creating patterns that support product growth.
Hoje, eu usaria esses aprendizados para: Today, I would use those lessons to take a larger role in product direction, exploring new features alongside improvements to existing ones. The experience reinforced the value of following design from user conversations through implementation.

O SEBRAE Paraná havia desenvolvido uma m: SEBRAE Paraná had developed a methodology to assess and strengthen innovation ecosystems in municipalities. The method was comprehensive, but applying it relied on forms, spreadsheets, and documents scattered across separate files.
Isso dificultava a colaboração, o acompa: This made collaboration, assessment tracking, and reporting difficult. Training new consultants was also demanding because the knowledge they needed was not always accessible during their work.
Meu papel foi entender a metodologia, or: My role was to understand the methodology, organize the experience, and design a platform for consultants and managers. The challenge was to make the work easier while preserving the method’s depth.
Comecei estudando o manual de aproximada: I started by studying the roughly 150-page manual, talking with the SEBRAE team, and reviewing their files and processes. I wanted to understand both the information they needed and how they used it.
Identifiquei dois perfis principais:: I identified two main user groups:
entrevistavam os atores dos ecossistemas: interviewed ecosystem stakeholders and completed assessments. They were the most frequent users.
acompanhavam o trabalho, consultavam rel: tracked the work, reviewed reports, and monitored how innovation ecosystems evolved.
Mapear a jornada do consultor ajudou a r: Mapping the consultant’s journey revealed an opportunity: even with a complex methodology, everyday work could be organized into a clear sequence.
A operação seguia um caminho relativamen: The work followed a relatively predictable path: select or create an assessment, collect information, enter the data, and calculate the score.
Organizei a interface em torno dessa seq: I organized the interface around that sequence, making one primary action clear in each context. Operational tasks took priority, while methodological explanations remained available as needed.
A expectativa era que os consultores gan: Consultants were expected to become familiar with the platform over time. Extensive content therefore did not need to compete with daily actions. Dashboards and analysis were more relevant to managers and received less emphasis in the data-entry flow.
Essa organização permitia avançar com ra: This organization allowed users to move quickly and consult the method’s details whenever a question arose.

A Sinapse Finance oferecia terceirização: Sinapse Finance provided outsourced financial operations for small and midsize businesses. Technology helped make those operations faster, more predictable, and easier to track.
Como designer principal, trabalhei em du: As the lead designer, I worked on two initiatives: a financial automation platform and improvements to the forms used to collect client information. I worked with a second designer transitioning from graphic design to UX, alongside the product owner, financial specialists, and developers. I also wrote HTML and CSS to support delivery.

Os usuários conheciam processos financei: Users were familiar with financial processes and digital tools. They wanted more control, transparency, and speed. My challenge was to turn complex rules into an experience they could understand and configure.
Os formulários haviam sido criados para: The forms had been created to standardize data entry. In practice, many clients preferred to send information through other channels or ask Sinapse consultants to fill them out.
Em alguns casos, fornecedores também par: In some cases, vendors were also involved, adding more intermediaries before the information reached the operations team. The tool ended up shifting work onto the team it was supposed to support.
Inicialmente, as reclamações pareciam re: At first, complaints seemed related to bugs in an implementation built under a tight deadline. The investigation revealed a broader problem.
Nas automações, comecei documentando os: For the automations, I began by documenting existing financial processes: rules, conditions, paths, errors, and possible states. There was little room to change these routines, so representing them accurately was important.
Validei o mapeamento com o PO, especiali: I validated the mapping with the product owner, financial specialists, and senior developers. Engineering participated from this stage, discussing possibilities, constraints, and the technical cost of alternatives.
Esse alinhamento ajudava a evitar que um: This alignment helped prevent poorly understood rules from becoming part of the interface and software.
O trabalho com formulários aconteceu em: The form work took approximately two weeks, including research, redesign, and an initial post-launch evaluation.
Comecei com testes e conversas com desen: I started with testing and conversations with developers. I found fields accepting invalid input, unclear validation, and data that could cause processing problems.
